agent_summary:
Tested session management on juice.lab.test (OWASP Juice Shop v20.2.0, plain HTTP only). 60 read-only requests; no writes (none allowed), no test accounts.

Session model established: stateless JWT carried in the Authorization: Bearer header. The REST/API tier reads the token only from that header — ?token= query and Cookie: token= both still return "No Authorization header". No Set-Cookie is issued anywhere (no pre-auth session id → no fixation surface); the `token` cookie exists only for the server-rendered Pug pages /profile and /dataerasure, set client-side by the SPA.

KEY FINDING (recorded as critical lead): the JWT verifier accepts alg:none unsigned tokens. On /rest/basket/1, no token and a malformed token and an HS256-with-bad-signature token all return 401, but a Bearer token with header {"alg":"none"} and an empty signature returns 200 with basket data — an authentication-bypass / session-forgery flaw. whoami still returned {} for the forged token, so a reviewer with an account should map full identity-propagation impact.

Other leads recorded: (1) cookie-authenticated state-changing forms /profile and /dataerasure with no observable anti-CSRF token (confirm SameSite/token with an account); (2) bearer tokens and deluxeToken credentials exposed/transmitted over plaintext HTTP, plus /rest/memories leaking real deluxeTokens and emails to anonymous users (hijacking enabler). Also noted for other lanes: /api/Quantitys, /api/Recycles, /api/Deliverys readable unauthenticated; open redirect at /redirect; verbose stack traces; open /metrics and /ftp.

Items done: 1 (schema), 2 (cookie attributes), 3 (fixation), 4 (exposed session variables), 5 (CSRF), 6 (logout — client-side only, no server invalidation, no logout route), 9 (hijacking/forgery).

Items left OPEN (cannot test read-only without an account/writes): 7 session timeout — no valid JWT obtainable to inspect exp; 8 session puzzling — requires authenticated multi-step reset flows; only observed that whoami leniently returns {} for invalid/forged tokens.

leads.title: [agent] Cookie-authenticated server-rendered forms (/profile, /dataerasure) lack anti-CSRF tokens; app served over plain HTTP

detail.text: The REST/API tier authenticates only via the Authorization: Bearer JWT (confirmed: ?token= and Cookie: token= both still return "No Authorization header was found"; a Bearer value is parsed by express-jwt). However the server-rendered Pug pages /profile (username change) and /dataerasure (GDPR data erasure) are authenticated via the `token` cookie — unauthenticated GETs return 500 "Blocked illegal activity" from userProfile.js:69 and dataErasure.js:62. These are state-changing POST forms authenticated by a cookie the browser sends automatically, which is the classic Juice Shop CSRF surface. The token cookie is set client-side by the SPA, so its SameSite attribute could not be observed over HTTP, and the whole app runs over plain HTTP (no HSTS, no Secure flag possible). A reviewer with a test account should log in, read the /profile and /dataerasure forms for a hidden anti-CSRF token field, and confirm the token cookie's SameSite value. Not submitted (writes not allowed).

leads.title: [agent] JWT verification accepts alg:none unsigned tokens — authentication bypass / session forgery

detail.text: Protected endpoints behind the express-jwt middleware accept a forged JWT using the "none" algorithm with no signature. Evidence on /rest/basket/1: no Authorization -> 401 "No Authorization header"; Bearer with a malformed token (aaa.bbb.ccc) -> 401 "Invalid token: no header in signature"; Bearer with an HS256 header + invalid signature (x60) -> 401; but Bearer with header {"alg":"none","typ":"JWT"} and payload {"data":{"email":"admin@juice-sh.op"}} and an EMPTY signature (x55) -> HTTP 200 returning basket JSON (1310 bytes). This means the signature is not verified for alg:none, so an attacker can mint arbitrary session tokens and pass the authentication middleware for any JWT-protected endpoint without credentials. Combined with /rest/memories disclosing real user emails, an attacker can forge a token for any user. Read-only reproduction; no data was modified. whoami (x58) still returned {} for the forged token, so identity propagation into every handler needs a reviewer with an account to map full impact, but the auth-middleware bypass itself is confirmed.

leads.title: [agent] Session bearer tokens and deluxeToken credentials transmitted/exposed over plaintext HTTP

detail.text: The host answers on plain HTTP only (nginx, no TLS, no Strict-Transport-Security header on any response). JWT session tokens are carried in the Authorization header and are therefore sent in cleartext, interceptable on the network (session hijacking). Compounding this, GET /rest/memories returns deluxeToken values (persistent membership bearer credentials) plus password hashes for multiple users with no authentication, giving an anonymous attacker reusable session/credential material directly. No Secure cookie flag is possible over HTTP.
